plan: Ten new items; every topic and choice set checked against the live bank (contrast-transition and 'Indeed'/'Moreover' sets avoided as used in 093/101/110 and 036/054). salient/parochial WIC, Pando structure, honeybee dance-learning inference (with a reversed-claim distractor), seed-storage data, Vesuvius autumn-date evidence, Neanderthal cave-art cross-text with a conditional key, Ramanujan contrast synthesis, 'At the same time' transition, affect/effect. Keys paraphrase rather than quote the texts.

passages.title: A striking feature
passages.text: The most ______ feature of the new library is its glass reading room, which juts out over the river and is the first thing visitors notice as they cross the bridge into town.

passages.title: A narrow program
passages.text: Critics called the festival's programming ______: nearly every film had been made in the host city, and only one of the forty screenings came from outside the region.

passages.title: One giant tree
passages.text: In central Utah grows a stand of about 47,000 quaking aspen trunks known as Pando. Genetic tests show that every trunk is part of a single organism connected by one root system, making Pando one of the heaviest living things known. The stand, however, is no longer replacing its aging trunks. Deer and cattle eat the young shoots that sprout from the roots, and in areas where these animals can graze, few new trunks survive to replace the old ones.

passages.title: Learning to dance
passages.text: Honeybees tell nestmates where to find food through a "waggle dance" whose angle and duration encode direction and distance. In one experiment, researchers raised colonies in which young bees could not watch older bees dance before dancing themselves. The first dances of these bees were more disordered than those of bees that had watched experienced dancers. With practice, their dances became more orderly, but their signals for distance remained less accurate throughout their lives. These results suggest that ______

passages.title: Seeds in storage
passages.text:
A seed bank tested how many seeds of one crop variety still germinated after ten years of storage at three temperatures.
Storage temperature | Seeds that germinated after 10 years
−18°C | 95%
4°C | 80%
20°C | 30%
The researchers concluded that seeds stored frozen kept nearly all their ability to germinate, while seeds kept at room temperature (about 20°C) lost most of it.

passages.title: When Vesuvius erupted
passages.text: For centuries, the eruption of Mount Vesuvius that buried Pompeii was dated to August 24, 79 CE, based on copies of a letter by the Roman writer Pliny the Younger. Some archaeologists have argued that the eruption actually happened in the autumn, perhaps in October, and that the date in the surviving copies of the letter was miscopied.

passages.title: Neanderthal art (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
For much of the twentieth century, many researchers held that Neanderthals lacked the capacity for symbolic thought, pointing to the absence of clear Neanderthal art. Cave paintings, they argued, appeared only after modern humans arrived in Europe.
Text 2
In 2018, a team dated thin mineral crusts that had formed over red markings in three Spanish caves. The crusts, and therefore the markings beneath them, were at least 64,000 years old—about 20,000 years before modern humans are thought to have reached the region. If the dates hold up, the markings must have been made by Neanderthals.

passages.title: Ramanujan
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Srinivasa Ramanujan was born in India in 1887.
• He had little formal training in advanced mathematics and largely taught himself.
• In 1913, he sent pages of his results to the Cambridge mathematician G. H. Hardy.
• Hardy invited him to Cambridge, where they worked together for several years.
• In 1918, Ramanujan was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society.

passages.title: Quieter buses
passages.text: The city's new electric buses are quieter and produce no exhaust on the street. ______ each one costs nearly twice as much to buy as the diesel bus it replaces, a difference the city expects to recover only gradually through lower fuel and repair costs.

passages.title: A small effect
passages.text: Despite predictions that the fare increase would drive riders away, the change had little ______ on the number of people using the subway each weekday.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: is the first thing visitors notice
candidates.explanation: A feature that stands out and is noticed first is "salient."

A.rationale: A feature that is the first thing visitors notice is not hidden.

B.rationale: Nothing suggests the reading room is temporary.

C.rationale: A glass room jutting over the river is the opposite of modest.

hints: Is the feature easy or hard to notice?
candidates.remember: Details later in the sentence define the blank.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
candidates.evidence: only one of the forty screenings came from outside the region
candidates.explanation: Programming focused almost entirely on local work is narrow in outlook: "parochial."

A.rationale: Films drawn almost entirely from one city are the opposite of a wide-ranging mix.

C.rationale: Nothing suggests the program was ambitious in scope.

D.rationale: The text describes a narrow focus, not a dispute.

hints: How wide was the range of films?
candidates.remember: Use the detail after the colon to define the blank.

candidates.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It introduces a remarkable organism and then describes a threat to its long-term survival.
choices.B: It describes a genetic test and then explains how scientists first developed the method.
choices.C: It compares Pando with several other large organisms and then ranks them by weight.
choices.D: It presents a debate about aspen trees and then resolves the debate with new evidence.

candidates.evidence: The stand, however, is no longer replacing its aging trunks.
candidates.explanation: The first part establishes Pando as a single, enormous organism; after "however," the text describes grazing that prevents new trunks from surviving.

B.rationale: The genetic test is mentioned only as evidence; its development is not discussed.

C.rationale: No other organisms are described or ranked.

D.rationale: No debate is presented; the text describes a finding and a problem.

strategy.explanation: Label each half of the text.

candidates.remember: "However" often marks the turn from description to problem.

candidates.stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: honeybees cannot learn to dance at all unless they watch older bees.
choices.B: the direction signal in the dance is learned, while the distance signal is fixed at birth.
choices.C: some features of the dance are refined by watching others, rather than being fully present from birth.
choices.D: practice alone allows bees to reach the same accuracy as those that watched others.

candidates.evidence: their signals for distance remained less accurate throughout their lives
candidates.explanation: Bees without models danced but less accurately, and practice fixed only part of the problem, so social learning refines at least some features of the dance.

A.rationale: The isolated bees did dance and improved with practice, so watching is not required to dance.

B.rationale: The distance signal was the part that stayed less accurate without models, which points the other way.

D.rationale: The isolated bees' distance signals stayed less accurate despite practice.

hints: What could practice fix, and what couldn't it?

strategy.explanation: Combine the early and later results before reading the choices.

candidates.remember: Avoid choices that overstate ("at all") or reverse the evidence.

author_checklist.hardness: Requires separating 'can dance' from 'dances accurately' and rejecting a reversed distractor.

candidates.stem: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers' conclusion?

choices.A: After ten years, 80% of seeds stored at 4°C germinated, compared with 30% of seeds stored at 20°C.
choices.B: After ten years, 95% of seeds stored at −18°C germinated, compared with only 30% of seeds stored at 20°C.
choices.C: After ten years, 95% of seeds stored at −18°C germinated, compared with 80% of seeds stored at 4°C.
choices.D: After ten years, seeds at all three storage temperatures germinated at rates of at least 30%.

candidates.evidence: seeds stored frozen kept nearly all their ability to germinate
candidates.explanation: The conclusion contrasts frozen and room-temperature seeds; B gives both: 95% versus 30%.

A.rationale: This compares refrigerated with room-temperature seeds; the conclusion concerns frozen seeds.

C.rationale: This leaves out the room-temperature seeds the conclusion describes.

D.rationale: This hides the differences the conclusion depends on.

hints: Which two conditions does the conclusion name?

strategy.explanation: Match each condition in the claim to a row.

candidates.remember: Check that the choice names the same conditions as the claim.

candidates.subskill: Command of evidence: textual (supporting a claim)
candidates.stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the archaeologists' argument?

choices.A: Pliny the Younger described a tall, dark cloud rising from the mountain on the day that the eruption began.
choices.B: Pompeii's streets were paved with large stones that showed deep ruts worn by generations of cart wheels.
choices.C: Many of Pompeii's buildings had been damaged by a strong earthquake about seventeen years before the eruption.
choices.D: A Pompeii wall bears a mid-October date written in charcoal, which fades within months, apparently from 79 CE.

candidates.evidence: the eruption actually happened in the autumn, perhaps in October
candidates.explanation: A date written in quickly fading charcoal must have been recent when the city was buried, so an October date points to an autumn eruption.

A.rationale: This describes the eruption but says nothing about its date.

B.rationale: This concerns the city's streets, not when the eruption occurred.

C.rationale: An earlier earthquake does not indicate the eruption's month.

hints: Which finding gives evidence about the time of year?

strategy.explanation: Ask which choice bears on the date at all.

candidates.remember: Support must bear on the specific claim, not just the topic.

author_checklist.hardness: Requires seeing why a fading medium makes the inscription's date informative.

candidates.stem: Based on the texts, how would the team in Text 2 most likely respond to the view described in Text 1?

choices.A: By arguing that, if their dates are accurate, the cave markings show that Neanderthals did produce symbolic images
choices.B: By agreeing that cave paintings appeared only after modern humans arrived, since the markings are red
choices.C: By arguing that modern humans reached Spain far earlier than other researchers believe
choices.D: By claiming that mineral crusts cannot be used to date any markings beneath them

candidates.evidence: If the dates hold up, the markings must have been made by Neanderthals.
candidates.explanation: Text 1 says Neanderthals lacked symbolic art; Text 2's dates place markings before modern humans arrived, so the team would argue Neanderthals made them, with the condition that the dates hold.

B.rationale: The color of the markings has no bearing on who made them; the dates are the team's evidence.

C.rationale: The team assumes the usual arrival date; that is why it attributes the markings to Neanderthals.

D.rationale: The team relies on exactly this dating method.

hints: Who could have made markings that old?

strategy.explanation: Identify the claim, then the counterevidence.

candidates.remember: Keep the conditional ("if the dates hold up") in the answer.

author_checklist.hardness: Requires reasoning from dating evidence to authorship while keeping the stated condition.

candidates.stem: The student wants to emphasize that Ramanujan won major recognition despite his limited formal training. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: In 1913, Ramanujan sent pages of his results to the Cambridge mathematician G. H. Hardy.
choices.B: Ramanujan, who was born in India in 1887, later worked with G. H. Hardy at Cambridge.
choices.C: Although he was largely self-taught, Ramanujan was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1918.
choices.D: Hardy invited Ramanujan to Cambridge, where the two worked together for several years.

candidates.evidence: He had little formal training in advanced mathematics
candidates.explanation: The goal pairs limited training with major recognition; C states both and links them with "Although."

A.rationale: This describes a letter, not his recognition or his training.

B.rationale: This mentions his work with Hardy but not his limited training or his recognition.

D.rationale: This describes the collaboration without the contrast the goal requires.

hints: Which choice names both the training and the recognition?

strategy.explanation: Check that both parts of the goal appear.

candidates.remember: A contrast goal needs both sides of the contrast.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
candidates.evidence: are quieter and produce no exhaust on the street
candidates.explanation: The first sentence lists advantages; the second adds a drawback. "At the same time" introduces a qualifying fact that holds alongside the first.

A.rationale: The higher price is not caused by the buses being quiet and clean.

B.rationale: The cost is not an example of the buses' quietness or cleanliness.

C.rationale: The second sentence does not summarize the first; it adds a drawback.

hints: Does the second sentence add a benefit or a drawback?
candidates.remember: "At the same time" can introduce a fact that complicates the previous one.

candidates.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
candidates.explanation: After "had little," a noun is needed; "effect" is the noun meaning result.

B.rationale: "Affect" is usually a verb; after "little," the sentence needs the noun "effect."

C.rationale: "Little effects" is not idiomatic; the singular noun is needed.

D.rationale: "Affected" is a verb form and cannot follow "had little."

hints: Is a noun or a verb needed here?

strategy.explanation: Look at the word before the blank.
